blueprint: 10 x 10 FAT in 9 of 11; all 7 modules in 10 of 11 FATs. Typical order Q1 M1 (architecture / data independence, 11 of 11), Q2-Q3 M2 (ER/EER, mapping, relational algebra), Q3-Q4 M3 (normalization), Q5-Q6 M4 (indexing / B+ tree, query optimisation), Q7-Q8 M5-M6 (transactions, serializability, 2PL), Q9-Q10 M6-M7 (concurrency, NoSQL/CAP), with 'Q9 a or b; Q10 a or b' in 3 of 11. No 2026-27 BCSE302L FAT exists in the corpus; 2026-27 evidence is CAT-1 D1 and D2 (your slot letter) plus 3 sister FATs (BACSE202 A1/A2, CBS1007 A2).
small_n_warning: No 2026-27 BCSE302L FAT exists (n_recent = 0 for the FAT formula). Use the 2026-27 CAT and sister-FAT columns as the recency signal. Probabilities are ranks, not calibrated chances.

Normalization (1NF-BCNF): 1NF step first moves the multivalued attribute (phone numbers) to its own table before 2NF/3NF; key splits marks 1NF 3, 2NF 3, 3NF 4
2NF question requires naming the candidate key AND each partial dependency
Schedules / conflict serializability: Besides the precedence graph, the key also computes final data values (A = 230, B = 415.2) and names the anomaly (dirty read / lost update)
Query processing / optimization: Push selections (and projections) below joins before drawing the optimised tree
Indexing / B+ tree: Insertion and deletion asked in the same question; key draws the tree after each phase
EER / specialization: Must state total/partial and disjoint/overlapping constraints explicitly
ER diagram design: Business rules encode participation ('at least one', 'may or may not'); show total vs partial participation
